prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the camera wearer pushes open a glass-panelled retail door within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m on the right in frames 1–3) to step past a companion on the left (~0.5–1.0 m away) into a shop interior containing hanging clothing racks on the left (~1.0–2.5 m) and a seated person near the back window (~3.0–4.0 m ahead, roughly 1.5–2.5 m behind the racks) next to white display shelves on the right. As the wearer advances forward and turns slightly right from frame 1 to frame 5, the bright door frame retreats out of view on the right, the close companion passes behind the left edge of the frame after frame 3, and the foreground clothing racks and seated person become unoccluded and slightly closer. The depth map clearly separates the foreground clothing racks, mid-ground display counter in the lower-left of frame 5 (~0.6 m), and the background wall and floor gradient even where motion blur softens the RGB image in frames 1 and 4. However, the map is unreliable on the glass door panel in frames 1–3, where it treats the transparent window (and the seated person ~3.5–4.0 m behind it in frame 3) as a solid flat surface at the ~0.4 m door depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map tracks people and objects across the doorway transition: a companion in dark clothing stands close on the far left (~0.5–1.0 m, partially cropped by the left border in frames 1–2 and passing closely on the left in frame 3), the camera wearer's own right hand and door edge appear at the bottom-right (~0.3–0.5 m in frames 2–3), and a second person sits ~3.0–4.0 m ahead in the shop interior facing and looking toward the camera wearer in frames 3–5 with their left arm resting on a white shelf within their reach. As the wearer enters the room, the foreground person on the left moves out of view after frame 3 while the seated person shifts from the upper-right (seen through the door glass in frame 3) toward the center-left in frame 4 and center in frame 5 as the camera pans right. The masks help isolate the silhouette of the seated person at ~3.0–4.0 m against the bright window backlight and cluttered racks, as well as the close companion's torso in frame 3 despite heavy RGB motion blur. However, the map is highly unreliable in class labels and boundaries: it mislabels the door frame and the wearer's hand as 'person' or 'laptop' in frames 1–2, misclassifies the hanging clothing racks (~1.0–2.0 m on the left) as a 'suitcase' in frames 3–4, Hallucinates a second 'person' mask on a pair of hanging jeans next to the seated person in frame 4, and misses the retail shelves and doors entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1 through 4 and detects only a single yellow body skeleton in frame 5 for the person seated ~3.0 m ahead in the center of the room in front of the windows. In frame 5, the skeleton shows this person's torso and head facing directly toward the camera wearer, with bent legs seated in a wide stance above the floor, their right hand resting near their right thigh, and their left arm extended outward to the right to rest within arm's reach on top of the adjacent white display block (~0.4 m to their left). Compared to the RGB image, the skeleton in frame 5 cleanly resolves the seated person's joint positions and limb angles despite dark clothing blending together against the bright window. However, the pose map is completely unreliable in frames 1–4, failing to detect the camera wearer's own right hand reaching for the door handle at the bottom (~0.3–0.5 m in frames 1–2), the close companion walking past on the left (~0.5–1.0 m in frames 1–3, whose upper body and head are partly out of view), the seated person visible in frames 3 and 4, and any magenta hand skeletons across all five frames.
